title: Minimum Information Security Standards and government prescripts
summary: Apply classification and handling decisions without confusing policy schemes, records duties or access authority.
outcomes: Distinguish MISS from the 2022 Directive's sensitivity scheme.
Govern physical and digital records through their lifecycle.

realExample.title: Home Affairs digitises civic records
realExample.documentedOutcome: The 8 July 2025 Home Affairs budget speech reported more than 49 million civic records digitised since 2023.
realExample.discussion: Use a completed digitisation programme to examine source identity, quality, access, storage and the continuing status of original records.
realExample.scope: Documented digitisation output; it does not establish automatic disposal authority or disclose the department's detailed security arrangements.

units.title: Classification is an accountable decision
objectives: Escalate reclassification and access requests correctly.

chapters.title: Keep two policy schemes distinct
chapters.bodyHtml:
MISS was approved by Cabinet as national information-security policy in 1996. Its classified-information scheme includes Restricted, Confidential, Secret and Top Secret. The 2022 DPSA information-security Directive describes Public, Confidential and Secret sensitivity categories. These are source-specific schemes; identical words do not justify silently substituting one for the other.

For an actual departmental record, establish the governing prescript, authorised classifier and local approved handling policy. Record the scheme as well as the label. If systems exchange information under different schemes, obtain a documented mapping and handling decision from the responsible authority rather than inventing an automatic equivalence.

The course uses the publicly available policy text. Some institutional names and operational references in historical documents have changed. Resolve current authority through the department's authorised security and legal functions; do not treat a historical agency name as a current contact instruction.

chapters.title: Use consequence and need-to-know
chapters.bodyHtml:
A classification decision should reflect the sensitivity and consequence described by the applicable scheme. MISS explicitly warns against using security measures to conceal maladministration, corruption or criminal conduct. Embarrassment or a desire to avoid scrutiny is not a sound substitute for the proper classification and access process.

Clearance and need-to-know answer different questions. A cleared person may still have no service reason to receive a particular record. Confirm both the appropriate authorisation and the specific work purpose. Seniority alone is not a universal access permission.

Make the decision usable: identify the record and version, source scheme, authorised decision maker, handling requirements and review trigger. If only part of a document is sensitive, the proper authority can assess how a public or redacted version should be produced under the applicable process.

chapters.title: Reclassification preserves lineage
chapters.bodyHtml:
A recipient who believes a classification is wrong should seek the authorised reclassification route. Do not erase the label in a personal copy and then circulate it as though the original authority changed its decision.

Preserve the source version and record who approved the change, when it took effect and which recipients need notice. The practical aim is that people handling different copies understand the same current decision without losing the earlier record.

A statutory access request remains a distinct legal process. Provide classification facts to the Information Officer and legal assessment; do not use a classroom label as a complete access refusal. Likewise, an access decision should specify the actual material released rather than silently changing every copy in the archive.

application.title: Resolve a classification conflict
application.instructionsHtml:
A fictional department receives a document marked Secret under MISS. Its new case system offers only Public, Confidential and Secret under its 2022 Directive implementation. A senior manager asks to email the document to an external consultant who has no recorded need-to-know.

Spend about 60 minutes preparing a handling decision and a system-mapping issue for the authorised owners.
application.deliverable: A handling record and a proposed mapping/escalation note.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Retain the original scheme, label and document version. Confirm the consultant's authorised work purpose and required access conditions before sharing.

Do not assume two Secret labels create a complete handling equivalence. Ask the proper authority to approve the mapping and associated controls.

Record the decision, recipients, review trigger and any authorised redacted version. A senior request alone does not remove the need-to-know assessment.

reflection.prompt: Where could your current software lose the name of the classification scheme while preserving only a label?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Explain how to retain both the source scheme and the authorised local handling decision.

quiz.title: Classification is an accountable decision — knowledge check

questions.name: M04-U01-Q01
questions.promptHtml: Which set belongs to the MISS classified-information scheme?

answers.textHtml: Restricted, Confidential, Secret and Top Secret
answers.feedbackHtml: Identify the actual scheme, not just familiar labels.

answers.textHtml: Public, Confidential and Secret only
answers.feedbackHtml: That is the distinct three-label scheme in the 2022 departmental directive, not the MISS set asked here.

answers.textHtml: Confidential, Secret and Top Secret only
answers.feedbackHtml: This omits Restricted from the MISS classified-information scheme.

answers.textHtml: Public, Internal, Confidential and Secret
answers.feedbackHtml: These labels do not reproduce the MISS set.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Identify the actual scheme, not just familiar labels.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q02
questions.promptHtml: Two systems both use the label Secret. What is still needed?

answers.textHtml: An authorised mapping of schemes and handling requirements
answers.feedbackHtml: Retain the scheme and the handling decision.

answers.textHtml: An assumption of complete equivalence
answers.feedbackHtml: The labels may sit in different schemes.

answers.textHtml: Removal of all labels
answers.feedbackHtml: That loses useful source information.

answers.textHtml: Automatic public release
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not follow from the matching word.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Retain the scheme and the handling decision.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q03
questions.promptHtml: A cleared official requests a record unrelated to their work. What further question matters?

answers.textHtml: Whether there is an authorised need-to-know
answers.feedbackHtml: Clearance and need-to-know are distinct.

answers.textHtml: Whether the person's seniority alone permits unrestricted access
answers.feedbackHtml: Seniority does not replace an authorised need-to-know.

answers.textHtml: Whether clearance is being treated as permission for every record at that level
answers.feedbackHtml: Clearance and a work-related need-to-know are distinct considerations.

answers.textHtml: Whether the request can bypass the usual authority because it is urgent
answers.feedbackHtml: Urgency requires the appropriate decision route, not an assumption of permission.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Clearance and need-to-know are distinct.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q04
questions.promptHtml: A manager wants a label applied solely to hide maladministration. What does MISS indicate?

answers.textHtml: Security measures must not be used for that concealment
answers.feedbackHtml: Classification must follow its proper purpose.

answers.textHtml: Apply the highest label whenever disclosure would embarrass management
answers.feedbackHtml: Embarrassment is not a proper basis for using security measures to conceal maladministration.

answers.textHtml: Treat the manager's ownership of the file as unlimited classification authority
answers.feedbackHtml: Information custody does not justify that prohibited purpose.

answers.textHtml: Remove the record from the official register instead of classifying it
answers.feedbackHtml: Avoiding the register does not resolve the improper concealment.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Classification must follow its proper purpose.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q05
questions.promptHtml: A recipient thinks the classification is wrong. What is the appropriate next step?

answers.textHtml: Seek authorised reclassification and preserve the decision history
answers.feedbackHtml: Change classification through the authorised route.

answers.textHtml: Erase the label on one copy
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not change the source decision.

answers.textHtml: Circulate it publicly to force review
answers.feedbackHtml: That bypasses authority.

answers.textHtml: Assume age automatically declassifies it
answers.feedbackHtml: The applicable review process must be checked.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Change classification through the authorised route.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q06
questions.promptHtml: What should a PAIA response consider beyond a confidentiality label?

answers.textHtml: The statutory access process and applicable grounds
answers.feedbackHtml: Provide relevant security facts to the authorised access process.

answers.textHtml: Only the departmental classification label, used as an automatic refusal
answers.feedbackHtml: The statutory process and grounds still apply.

answers.textHtml: Only the technical custodian's personal view of disclosure risk
answers.feedbackHtml: The request must follow the authorised statutory route.

answers.textHtml: Only whether the requester has used the department's preferred informal channel
answers.feedbackHtml: An informal preference does not replace the applicable access process.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Provide relevant security facts to the authorised access process.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which fields preserve a classification decision? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Record version and source scheme
answers.feedbackHtml: They identify what was classified under which rules.

answers.textHtml: Authorised decision maker and review trigger
answers.feedbackHtml: They make changes accountable.

answers.textHtml: An encryption product name used as the sole explanation of classification
answers.feedbackHtml: Encryption does not record the classification authority, scheme or rationale.

answers.textHtml: A current label overwritten without identifying who changed it or why
answers.feedbackHtml: This loses the decision history needed to understand its authority.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A label should remain connected to its authority and object.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which statements correctly use historical MISS text? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Retain its status as a Cabinet-approved policy source
answers.feedbackHtml: That identifies its authority.

answers.textHtml: Resolve current institutional responsibilities through authorised channels
answers.feedbackHtml: Historical names may need a current mapping.

answers.textHtml: Treat every historical agency name as today's contact
answers.feedbackHtml: That may be inaccurate.

answers.textHtml: Treat the policy as an ISO certification
answers.feedbackHtml: These are different instruments.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Read both source authority and present implementation context.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q09
questions.promptHtml: Clearance automatically creates a need-to-know for every classified record.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. The specific authorised work purpose still matters.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: The specific authorised work purpose still matters.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The specific authorised work purpose still matters.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q10
questions.promptHtml: An approved redacted release should identify the actual version released.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This preserves the relationship between the source record and the authorised disclosure.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. This preserves the relationship between the source record and the authorised disclosure.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: This preserves the relationship between the source record and the authorised disclosure.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match each term to its decision role.

pairs.answer: Rules under which the label is assigned
Role permitted to change the decision

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The complete handling decision needs each element.

questions.name: M04-U01-Q12
questions.promptHtml: Retain the classification [[1]] as well as the [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A label without its source scheme can be ambiguous.

units.title: Handle records throughout their lifecycle
objectives: Apply controlled receipt, copying and transfer.
Join physical, digital and personnel controls.
Distinguish preservation copies, access copies and authorised disposal.

chapters.title: Receipt and transfer are part of the record
chapters.bodyHtml:
At receipt, confirm the intended recipient, completeness and applicable handling instruction. Record where the item will be held and who may use it. For controlled material, a copy or transfer should remain connected to its original identity and distribution decision.

An encrypted transfer does not by itself establish that the recipient was authorised. Conversely, a correct recipient does not make an unsuitable channel safe. Consider identity, purpose, channel, completeness and acknowledgement together.

Do not put real classified or personal records into this course's exercises. Practise the decision process with fictional titles and harmless sample material. The skill being assessed is accountable handling, not access to sensitive operational details.

chapters.title: Physical and digital controls work together
chapters.bodyHtml:
A controlled database can still be undermined by an unattended printout, an unlocked archive room or an unrecorded removable copy. Match physical storage and movement controls to the applicable handling requirements, and make staff responsibilities clear.

Join access changes to personnel events. A transferring employee may retain a physical key, an offline copy and a supplier login even after the main account changes. Review the whole information-handling relationship rather than a single technical account.

Incident reporting should be usable when a device or document is lost. Record the item, last known custody, information involved and containment actions without broadcasting the sensitive content. Preserve the facts needed for the authorised investigation and notification decisions.

chapters.title: Digitisation and disposal require separate decisions
chapters.bodyHtml:
The Home Affairs digitisation outcome illustrates the scale at which paper records can become digital service assets. In a migration, retain source identity, capture quality, version and a way to locate the original. A scan that cannot be connected to the correct person or record series may be unusable even if its image is clear.

Distinguish a preservation master from a lower-bandwidth access copy. The access copy may be convenient for service delivery; the master may retain details needed for long-term preservation. Record the relationship and permissions instead of treating them as unrelated files.

Disposal is a separate authorised action. Confirm the applicable records schedule, written authority and preservation requirements before destroying paper or digital copies. Keep an appropriate disposal record. A supplier's storage-cost concern can prompt review, but it does not itself create disposal authority.

application.title: Plan a controlled records digitisation batch
application.instructionsHtml:
A fictional provincial archive will scan 500 permit files. Staff propose naming scans by applicant surname, placing all images on a shared folder and destroying the originals once scanning ends.

Spend about 60 minutes preparing a revised batch plan covering identification, quality, access, transfer and disposal.
application.deliverable: A batch-control sheet and handling procedure.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Use stable record identifiers and a source-to-scan index; surnames alone can collide. Check page completeness and legibility against the original, including exceptions.

Assign authorised access and controlled transfer. Preserve a master/access-copy relationship where needed and keep physical originals in their authorised custody.

Obtain and apply the actual disposal authority separately. A completed scan count is not a disposal decision.

reflection.prompt: Which records movement in your department produces a copy without a clear owner?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Describe a practical way to retain its purpose, custody and disposal decision.

quiz.title: Handle records throughout their lifecycle — knowledge check

questions.name: M04-U02-Q01
questions.promptHtml: A transfer is encrypted. What must still be confirmed?

answers.textHtml: The recipient's identity, authority and purpose
answers.feedbackHtml: Secure transfer includes more than encryption.

answers.textHtml: Only that the transport negotiated encryption successfully
answers.feedbackHtml: Protected transport does not determine the recipient's authority or the permitted purpose.

answers.textHtml: Only that the message reached a departmental-looking address
answers.feedbackHtml: Delivery and appearance do not establish the specific recipient's permission.

answers.textHtml: Only that the file cannot be opened without a password
answers.feedbackHtml: Password protection does not by itself authorise the recipient's use.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Secure transfer includes more than encryption.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q02
questions.promptHtml: Why is surname-only naming weak for a digitisation batch?

answers.textHtml: Different records can share the same surname and lose source identity
answers.feedbackHtml: Use stable identifiers linked to the source record.

answers.textHtml: Because an OCR search always supplies a unique record identity
answers.feedbackHtml: Searchable text can still contain identical names and does not replace a stable index.

answers.textHtml: Because the scan date alone always distinguishes every original
answers.feedbackHtml: Several records may share both name and scan date.

answers.textHtml: Because a digital folder automatically preserves all source relationships
answers.feedbackHtml: A folder structure does not necessarily retain each source-to-scan identity.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Use stable identifiers linked to the source record.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q03
questions.promptHtml: What does a completed scan count prove?

answers.textHtml: How many items were reported captured within the count's scope
answers.feedbackHtml: Keep volume, quality, access and disposal claims separate.

answers.textHtml: Every image is complete and correct
answers.feedbackHtml: Quality needs its own evidence.

answers.textHtml: Every original may be destroyed
answers.feedbackHtml: Disposal authority is separate.

answers.textHtml: All access is authorised
answers.feedbackHtml: Permissions need assessment.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Keep volume, quality, access and disposal claims separate.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q04
questions.promptHtml: An employee changes role. Which access may remain outside the main account?

answers.textHtml: Physical keys, offline copies and supplier logins
answers.feedbackHtml: Review the complete information-handling relationship.

answers.textHtml: Only permissions listed in the central directory, because all other access expires automatically
answers.feedbackHtml: Physical and external access may have separate lifecycles.

answers.textHtml: Only the permissions requested for the new role
answers.feedbackHtml: The review must also consider old access outside the main account.

answers.textHtml: Only the account's password, because changing it revokes every retained copy
answers.feedbackHtml: A password change does not recall offline information or physical keys.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Review the complete information-handling relationship.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q05
questions.promptHtml: What should govern destruction of scanned originals?

answers.textHtml: The applicable records schedule, disposal authority and preservation requirements
answers.feedbackHtml: Digitisation and disposal are distinct decisions.

answers.textHtml: The scanner operator's preference
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not establish authority.

answers.textHtml: A storage-cost complaint alone
answers.feedbackHtml: Cost can prompt review, not authorise disposal.

answers.textHtml: An automatic rule that digital replaces paper
answers.feedbackHtml: That does not follow.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Digitisation and disposal are distinct decisions.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q06
questions.promptHtml: A sensitive document is lost. What is a useful initial report?

answers.textHtml: Its identity, last known custody, information scope and containment facts
answers.feedbackHtml: Provide enough facts for the authorised response while limiting disclosure.

answers.textHtml: The full document sent to all staff
answers.feedbackHtml: That can create further disclosure.

answers.textHtml: A guess that no harm is possible
answers.feedbackHtml: The scope needs assessment.

answers.textHtml: No report until it is found
answers.feedbackHtml: Delay can impede containment.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Provide enough facts for the authorised response while limiting disclosure.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which controls help a digitisation batch? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: A source-to-scan index
answers.feedbackHtml: It preserves lineage.

answers.textHtml: Completeness and legibility checks
answers.feedbackHtml: They assess whether the capture is usable.

answers.textHtml: Overwriting duplicates without review
answers.feedbackHtml: It can lose distinct records.

answers.textHtml: Destroying originals before authority is checked
answers.feedbackHtml: It can breach retention requirements.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Preserve source identity and quality before later decisions.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which statements distinguish preservation and access copies? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: They can serve different purposes
answers.feedbackHtml: Convenience and long-term preservation may differ.

answers.textHtml: Their relationship and permissions should be retained
answers.feedbackHtml: This supports trustworthy use.

answers.textHtml: An access copy automatically replaces every master
answers.feedbackHtml: That is not necessarily true.

answers.textHtml: Copies never need owners
answers.feedbackHtml: They still require handling decisions.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Treat related copies as a managed record family.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q09
questions.promptHtml: Physical controls remain relevant when the main application has strong access controls.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Printouts, keys and storage areas can expose the same information.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Printouts, keys and storage areas can expose the same information.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Printouts, keys and storage areas can expose the same information.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q10
questions.promptHtml: Real classified records are necessary to demonstrate the handling principles in this course.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Fictional harmless materials can exercise the decision process.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: Fictional harmless materials can exercise the decision process.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Fictional harmless materials can exercise the decision process.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match each control to its purpose.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: These controls cover different lifecycle stages.

questions.name: M04-U02-Q12
questions.promptHtml: A scan's quality and the original's [[1]] authority are [[2]] decisions.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Capture success does not decide disposal.
